summary:
Public Law 118-106, the "Confirmation Of Congressional Observer Access Act of 2024" (or "COCOA Act of 2024"), amends Title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA) (52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.) to establish a statutory requirement that States provide designated congressional election observers with access to observe election administration procedures in elections for Federal office. 

Section 2(a) of the Act redesignates HAVA sections 304 and 305 as sections 305 and 306 (52 U.S.C. 21084, 21085) and inserts a new Section 304 (52 U.S.C. 21083a note). New Section 304(a) sets forth a congressional finding of constitutional authority under Article I, Section 5, Clause 1 and Article I, Section 4, Clause 1, clarifying that the statutory procedures do not establish new constitutional authorities but serve as a convenient reference for existing congressional observation powers.

Under Section 304(b), States must provide "designated congressional election observers" with full access to observe all elements of election administration, including pre- and post-election procedures, and any area where ballots are cast, processed, scanned, tabulated, canvassed, recounted, audited, or certified. Section 304(b)(2) prohibits observers from handling ballots or election equipment, advocating for candidates or positions, reducing ballot secrecy or voter privacy, or interfering with voters or election administrators. A rule of construction in Section 304(b)(3) clarifies that observers are not prohibited from asking questions of election officials, workers, or other State or local officials.

Section 304(c) governs the removal of observers. Under Section 304(c)(1)(A), a State or local election official may remove an observer if there is a "reasonable basis to believe" the observer has engaged in, or will imminently engage in, unlawful intimidation, deceptive practices, or disruption of election procedures. The mere presence of an observer does not constitute a reasonable basis for removal. Upon removal, the election official must, within a 24-hour statutory deadline, inform the chair and ranking minority member of the House Committee on House Administration or the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, as applicable, and provide written notice detailing the reasons for removal. Section 304(c)(3) permits the respective committee chair or ranking minority member to designate a replacement observer for the remaining duration of the observation.

Section 304(d) defines a "designated congressional election observer" as a House or Senate employee designated in writing by the chair or ranking minority member of the House Committee on House Administration or the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration (or successor committees) to gather information, including for contested elections. Section 304(e) defines "State" to include the 50 States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

Section 2(b) of the Act makes a conforming amendment to HAVA's civil enforcement provision (Section 401, 52 U.S.C. 21111) by striking "and 303" and inserting "303, and 304", thereby extending HAVA's existing enforcement mechanisms to the new observer access requirements. Section 2(c) executes clerical amendments to the HAVA table of contents.
